description.comment: The least weasel (Mustela nivalis), little weasel, common weasel, or simply weasel is the smallest member of the genus Mustela, family Mustelidae and order Carnivora. It is native to Eurasia, North America and North Africa, and has been introduced to New Zealand, Malta, Crete, the Azores, and Sao Tome. It is classified as least concern by the IUCN, due to its wide distribution and large population throughout the Northern Hemisphere. Eighteen subspecies are recognized (from Wikipedia entry). This sample of a male individual of the vulgaris subspecies caught near Brook Waimarama Sanctuary in Whakatu Nelson, New Zealand was collected and prepared by Alex Leonard, Robert Schadewinkel, and Andrew J. Veale and coordinated by James Russell of the University of Auckland to generate a high-quality reference genome for the Vertebrate Genomes Project (VGP). The body has been accessioned at the Auckland War Memorial Museum. Sequencing and genome assembly were conducted at the Vertebrate Genome Lab (VGL) at the Rockefeller University, led by Erich D. Jarvis, Giulio Formenti, and Jennifer Balacco.

assembly_info.comments: Curator note: This assembly is very fragmented and contains a high amount of repeat content. We cannot be sure of the order or orientation of the following regions: Chromosome 8, haplotype 1 and haplotype 2, between 52.1- 59.2Mbp; chromosome 5, haplotype 1 and haplotype 2, between 27.3- 42.6Mbp; chromosome 2, haplotype 1 and haplotype 2, between 65.4- 73.6Mbp and 95.4- 108.9Mbp; chromosome 3, haplotype 1 and haplotype 2, between 11.4- 18.6Mbp; chromosome 7, haplotype 1 and haplotype 2, between 14.3- 21.8Mbp; chromosome 14, haplotype 1 and haplotype 2, between 22.5- 25.4Mbp; chromosome 15, haplotype 1 only, between 62.9- 67.0Mbp
